description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of responses across four categories — “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding,” and “Journalism” — based on the extent to which conversations were perceived as “Partially” (red), “No” (green), or an unlabeled yellow category (likely “Yes” or “Fully,” inferred from context and legend placement) in relation to social engineering susceptibility or detection. The horizontal axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” ranging from 0 to 60, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each category has three horizontal bars stacked vertically, with red (Partially) consistently being the longest bar across all categories, indicating the highest number of conversations falling into that response. For “Academic Collaboration,” red extends to approximately 58, yellow to ~20, and green to ~8. For “Recruitment,” red reaches ~55, yellow ~22, and green ~9. In “Academic Funding,” red is ~50, yellow ~12, and green ~5. For “Journalism,” red is ~45, yellow ~35, and green ~10. The chart suggests that across all domains, a majority of conversations were perceived as only partially susceptible or detectable, with “Journalism” showing the highest proportion of fully susceptible (yellow) conversations. The legend is partially cut off but clearly associates red with “Partially,” yellow with an implied “Yes” or “Fully,” and green with “No.” The chart is tilted diagonally in the image, but the data remains interpretable.
